title: Benny at Lucky Star mixed up two scratch cards. Yours is a C$200 winner. The lady before you got the dud.

outcomes.text: Benny runs out to the sidewalk and catches her. She screams, he screams, a pigeon screams. She hugs you twice.

later.text: Remember the scratch card mix-up at Lucky Star? The lady came back with a tray of homemade dumplings and C$40 'for the honest one.'

outcomes.text: You catch her at the bus stop. 'Half each?' She thinks, then laughs. 'Half each.' Benny calls it 'the Flushing compromise.'
You scratch, you win, you smile at Benny. Benny, who has never bought a ticket, smiles back. He doesn't know yet.

later.text: Remember Benny's scratch card mix-up? The lady came back with her receipt. Benny paid her from his own pocket, and now he 'can't find' your favorite card.

title: A scratched card on Lucky Star's floor. Whoever dropped it didn't check the back: it's a C$150 winner.

outcomes.text: Six people claim it. Benny asks what game it was. Only an old man in a Meteors cap gets it right. He kisses the card.

later.text: Remember finding the C$150 card on Lucky Star's floor? The man in the Meteors cap left C$40 with Benny 'for the one who asked around.'

outcomes.text: Benny tapes it to the register: 'Is this yours? Prove it.' The crowd at Lucky Star loves a mystery.
Finders keepers, the oldest law in Queens. C$150. Somebody out there thinks they lost.

title: Dev from the gym asks to borrow C$300 'until Friday.' Dev said that last Friday too.

outcomes.text: You hand Dev C$300. He hugs you so hard you hear your back realign.

later.text: Remember lending Dev C$300 'until Friday'? He paid it all back with C$30 on top and a protein shake that tastes like chalk.

outcomes.text: You lend Dev C$300. He promises Friday, then promises the gym owner he'll fix the leg press.

later.text: Remember lending Dev C$300 'until Friday'? It's been a few Fridays. He waves at you from across the gym, very warmly.

outcomes.text: 'Half, and you pay me Friday.' Dev salutes. You've drawn a line, and it's made of money.

later.text: Remember lending Dev C$150? He paid it back, a week late, in crumpled fives. 'Told you Friday.' It was not Friday.

outcomes.text: 'I can't, Dev.' He nods. He's heard it before. You do squats next to each other in a silence you can feel in your legs.
'Man, I'm broke too.' Dev hugs you in solidarity. Then you buy a C$9 smoothie at the gym bar, in front of him.

title: Sal's nephew Karim at the deli: 'C$200 till my DJ gig pays. Uncle Sal can't know.'

options.label: Lend it, keep the secret
options.cost: C$200 and a secret from Sal

outcomes.text: You slip Karim C$200 behind the chip rack. The cat sees. The cat says nothing. For now.

later.text: Remember lending Karim C$200 behind Sal's back? His DJ gig paid. He paid you back, plus a spot on his guest list. Sal still doesn't know.

outcomes.text: You lend it and tell Sal. Sal sighs a sigh from 1998 and makes Karim mop to pay off the 'interest.'

later.text: Remember telling Sal about Karim's C$200 loan? Sal paid you back himself, the next morning, with a sandwich. Karim still owes Sal.

outcomes.text: 'Sorry, Karim.' He shrugs and asks the next customer. Sal, from the register, says 'good' without looking up.
